subject: SECR error: Multiple session time varying covariates

messages.author: 2355879d46fd3735
messages.subject: SECR error: Multiple session time varying covariates
parts:
Hi all.
I'm getting the following error when attempting to model detection as function of time varying trap covariates in a multiple session model:
Error in `[<-`(`*tmp*`, 1:dimx[1], 1:dimx[2], value = x) : subscript out of bounds

My msCapthist object combines observation data for three years (sessions) and three trap files since usage varies by year. I then added covariates for each session.  

covariates(traps(NerCH[[1]])) <- TimeCovsTraps2016
covariates(traps(NerCH[[2]])) <- TimeCovsTraps2017
covariates(traps(NerCH[[3]])) <- TimeCovsTraps2018

My covariates are indexed in the msCapthist object. I'm only using a single covariate in this example.

timevaryingcov(traps(NerCH[[1]])) <- list(YDay = 3:53) 
timevaryingcov(traps(NerCH[[2]])) <- list(YDay = 3:53)
timevaryingcov(traps(NerCH[[3]])) <- list(YDay = 3:53)

I have no issue fitting models without time varying covariates, but when I try to call on YDay I get the above error. I was able to work around the issue by specifying timecov within the model. However, I would like to add further covariates and fit them independently if possible.

Thanks,

Josh

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: SECR error: Multiple session time varying covariates
parts:
Hi Josh
I think you've been caught by the 'fastproximity' monster. By default, secr.fit collapses multi-occasion proximity data to a single occasion to speed up processing. This has many unwelcome consequences - one obviously being that you can no longer model occasion-specific effects. If I'm right, the 'easy' answer is to set details = list(fastproximity = FALSE), but you'll notice it's slow.

In general, I think you'll find time-varying trap covariates are more trouble than they're worth, but they're there for the brave.
Murray
